Uomo di 70 anni. Gastroscopia con biopsi: 70-year-old man. Gastroscopy with biopsy: signet ring cell gastric adenocarcinoma. Chest-abdomen-pelvis CT with intravenous and oral contrast for staging.
Referta in ordine: stomaco, linfonodi, c: Report in order: stomach, lymph nodes, conclusion.
Nel carcinoma gastrico la TC serve sopra:
In gastric carcinoma, CT is mainly used to look for lymph nodes and metastases; T stage is better assessed with the stomach distended (water or gas) and with endoscopic ultrasound.
Signs to look for: focal or diffuse wall thickening (over 1 cm with the stomach distended), mucosal enhancement, irregularity of the serosal contour and stranding in the perigastric fat (T4a, serosal involvement), infiltration of neighboring organs (T4b: pancreas, transverse colon, liver).
The signet ring cell (diffuse) type tends to infiltrate the wall without forming a mass: the stomach may become rigid and poorly distensible ("linitis plastica") and often causes peritoneal carcinomatosis, which CT underestimates; for this reason staging laparoscopy is performed before surgery.
Lymph nodes: perigastric, subpyloric stations, along the left gastric artery, common hepatic, celiac, splenic; para-aortic nodes are distant metastases (M1).
Carcinoma gastrico diffuso: la TC sottos: Diffuse gastric carcinoma: CT underestimates the peritoneum; staging laparoscopy before surgery.
Adenocarcinoma gastrico a cellule ad ane: Signet ring cell gastric adenocarcinoma, stage IV (T4 N3 M1) in the TCGA clinical data of the TCGA-STAD collection; the site of the metastases is not stated.
